title: Business Requirements Document — Hospital Patient Portal

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body: The Hospital Patient Portal is designed to provide secure, compliant digital access to patient health information, appointment scheduling, and communication with healthcare providers. This document outlines the business requirements necessary to ensure the system meets healthcare industry standards, specifically adhering to HIPAA, GDPR (if applicable to EU patients), HL7 FHIR, and DICOM frameworks. The strategic rationale for this portal is to enhance patient engagement, reduce administrative overhead, and ensure robust data security and privacy.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body: The primary business objectives include improving patient satisfaction through self-service capabilities, ensuring strict compliance with healthcare data protection regulations, and optimizing operational efficiency. Success metrics will be defined based on user adoption rates, system uptime, compliance audit results, and reduction in manual administrative tasks. Specific metrics will be established in collaboration with stakeholders to align with organizational goals.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries (In/Out of Scope)
sections.body: In Scope: Secure patient authentication, access to medical records, appointment scheduling, and secure messaging with healthcare providers. Out of Scope: Clinical decision support systems, electronic health record (EHR) management, and billing/payment processing. The operational boundaries will be further defined in subsequent documentation phases to ensure alignment with organizational capabilities and regulatory requirements.

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body: Key stakeholders include patients, healthcare providers, IT security teams, compliance officers, and hospital administrators. Governance personas will be established to oversee system development, ensure regulatory compliance, and manage stakeholder communications. Specific roles and responsibilities will be detailed in the governance framework document.

sections.title: 5. Business Requirements Specification Matrix
table: Implement multi-factor authentication for patient access to the portal.
Patients can securely log in using multi-factor authentication; unauthorized access attempts are logged and blocked.
Provide patients with secure access to their medical records, including lab results and discharge summaries.
Patients can view and download their medical records; access is logged and auditable.
Enable patients to schedule, reschedule, and cancel appointments online.
Patients can successfully schedule appointments; changes are reflected in the provider's calendar.
Allow secure, encrypted messaging between patients and healthcare providers.
Messages are encrypted in transit and at rest; delivery and read receipts are available.
Ensure all data handling practices comply with HIPAA regulations.
System passes HIPAA compliance audit; all PHI is encrypted and access is restricted to authorized personnel.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body: Assumptions include that patients have access to the internet and a compatible device, and that healthcare providers will actively use the portal for communication. Operational constraints include the need for continuous system availability, strict data encryption standards (AES-256 for PHI at rest), and adherence to recovery time objectives (RTO < 1h) and recovery point objectives (RPO < 5min). These constraints will be validated during the system design phase.

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body: The risk baseline includes potential data breaches, non-compliance with healthcare regulations, and system downtime. Mitigation strategies involve implementing robust encryption, regular security audits, and disaster recovery plans. The compliance baseline is anchored in HIPAA, GDPR (if applicable), HL7 FHIR, and DICOM standards, ensuring that all data handling, transmission, and storage practices meet the highest industry benchmarks.
